annotation.title_clean: An Act Concerning the Regulation of Aeronautics; To Restrict the Use of Unmanned Aircraft Systems Under Certain Circumstances (Arkansas HB 1770, Act 1019)
annotation.title_en: An Act Concerning the Regulation of Aeronautics; To Restrict the Use of Unmanned Aircraft Systems Under Certain Circumstances (Arkansas HB 1770, Act 1019)
annotation.summary_en: Arkansas Act 1019 (HB 1770, 2015) makes it a misdemeanor to knowingly use an unmanned aircraft system to surveil or record critical infrastructure without the owner's written consent, with exemptions for federal, state, emergency and FAA-authorized use, and creates civil damages of at least $10,000, trebled where the violation yields profit.
key_provisions_or_claims: Offense of unlawful use of an unmanned aircraft system over critical infrastructure without owner consent
Class B misdemeanor; Class A for repeat offenses
Exemptions for federal/state contractors, FAA certificate holders, emergency agencies, and own-property use
Civil liability: greater of actual damages or $10,000, treble damages for profit, plus attorney's fees
Critical infrastructure defined as power systems, refineries, chemical facilities and storage
